title: ObservationTask
description: One leased observation pass, returned by the control plane in the 200 response of POST /api/v1/gateways/{id}/tasks/claim. It carries identifiers only. It never carries a URL, namespace, object name, credential, header, command or secret value. The Gateway resolves each connector_id and target_id against its own local configuration and refuses anything it does not recognise.

task_id.description: Stable id of the observation task (observation_tasks.id). One task per (request, binding). Survives re-claims.

attempt_id.description: Fencing token (observation_tasks.current_attempt_id). A new value is minted on every claim. Only the current attempt_id may renew, release or submit a result, and only while its lease is live.

attempt_count.description: Number of claims handed out for this task, including this one (observation_tasks.attempt_count).

lease_expires_at.description: Control-plane clock. After this instant the attempt can no longer renew or submit, and another replica may claim the task with a new attempt_id.

deadline_at.description: Control-plane clock. After this instant the control plane closes the task as timed_out. A lease never extends past the deadline.

request_id.description: The secret change request this observation belongs to (access_requests.id).

correlation_id.description: sync_jobs.correlation_id of the job that executed the change, for audit joins.

skew_margin_seconds.description: Base clock-skew margin the control plane will apply. The Gateway uses it to propose stage outcomes. The control plane recomputes outcomes with the measured offsets reported in the result.

connector_refs.description: One entry per expected stage. At most one entry per stage; the control plane enforces that, the Gateway refuses duplicates with schema_violation.

rollout_baseline.description: Optional. Copied by the control plane from the earliest accepted pass of this task in which eso_sync was observed. Lets a stateless Gateway detect a rollout that reused an older ReplicaSet (revision annotation bumped after that pass). Null or absent until such a pass exists.

localId.description: An identifier defined in the Gateway's local configuration, advertised through PUT /catalog and bound by an admin in the control plane. Lowercase DNS-label style, so it cannot hold a URL, path, namespace separator or credential.

gateway_id.description: Logical Gateway the task is routed to. Must equal the {id} in the request path and the authenticated Gateway.

environment_id.description: The environment of the binding that produced this task (gateway_connector_bindings.environment_id). Informational for the Gateway.

connector_id.description: Local connector name bound to this Gateway, for example eso-main, rollout-main or argocd-main (gateway_connectors.name).

target_id.description: Target inside that connector, for example payments-api. The Gateway maps it to a namespace and object name from its own configuration.

provider_type.description: Values match storage.ProviderConnectionType. Only providers with a core implementation are listed for v1.

provider_version_id.description: Provider-assigned version id the agent recorded on write: the AWS Secrets Manager VersionId, or the Vault KV v2 version number as a decimal string. Null when the agent did not report one, or reported an empty id (Vault KV v1). Never a hash of the value.

provider_version_at.description: Creation time of that version as reported by the agent. For AWS Secrets Manager this is the agent clock at write time; for Vault it is the server created_time when present. Informational; ordering uses executed_at.

version_source.description: Where provider_version_id came from. none means provider_version_id is null and the task verdict cannot be above partially_observed.

executed_at.description: Control-plane clock time at which the control plane recorded the job as succeeded. Lower bound for ordering. Evidence observed at or before executed_at plus skew cannot relate to this change.

provider_connection_id.description: Provider connection of the written secret when the control plane knows it (always for cross-team requests; for patch requests only when the request resolves to one). Informational for the Gateway.

name.description: Provider-side secret name or KV path. Used only to compare with ExternalSecret remoteRef.key inside the Gateway. It is never dialled. No scheme separators allowed.

deployment_revision.description: deployment.kubernetes.io/revision reported in that earlier pass.
